mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% combined with a federal funds rate below 2% for three months signals a high-inflation low-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 200000 for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -2% for four consecutive months, regardless of GDP trend, signals weakening consumer demand and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -2% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
